docs.title: API conventions
docs.text: This chapter covers SDK subscriptions, caches, Actions and synchronous Services. Classes are in namespace north. Declarations and public data types follow; include <north_sdk/NorthSDK.h> when compiling an application.

docs.title: Common parameters and results
docs.text:
Object Usage rule Status SDK result for connect and Actions; check ok()/bool Result<T> Check bool before value; on failure inspect error.code/message BasicResponse After Result succeeds, check success and message MasterResponse Check result against kOk; before/after are service snapshots Header stamp_ns is source time and system_time_ns is remote system time; their domains may differ. seq is a sequence number, key identifies the source, and frame_id identifies a source or coordinate frame. Side kLeft/kRight; Python LEFT/RIGHT; invalid values are rejected

Default units are SI: m, rad, m/s, rad/s, N, Nm, A and V, with temperature in degrees Celsius. Time fields use explicit _ns/_ms/_s units; power clocks use clock_domain. Arrays use fixed device joint order and quaternion fields are w/x/y/z.

These rules apply to state/event subscriptions using SubscribeOptions and to latest_* cache reads. See VideoClient and AlignmentClient for their specialized options.

Common parameter Type, default and rules callback Required, nonempty C++ std::function<void(const T&)> or Python callable. The C++ reference is callback-scoped; copy data needed afterward. options SubscribeOptions, default DropOldest; controls local callback queuing. Python defaults to SubscribeOptions(). max_age / max_age_ms Required C++ milliseconds; Python int defaults to 1000 ms. Must be nonnegative. Measures elapsed time since SDK reception on this computer, independently of message timestamps.

Retain the subscription returned by on_*. Destruction, close(), or leaving a Python subscription context cancels it. SDK worker callbacks should remain short; no new callback starts after close() returns.

latest_* automatically receives state and returns a cached copy without a prior subscription. Missing or expired samples return kStaleState, negative age returns kInvalidArgument. Choose the age from the device publication period and application latency requirements. C++ checks Result<T>; Python returns data or raises NorthSDKError.

docs.text: Field Default Meaning zenoh_config_path Empty Native Zenoh configuration file connect_endpoints {} Supply endpoints explicitly or through the file connect_timeout 5000 ms Wait for one communication-session connection attempt service_timeout 6000 ms Ordinary service wait configuration master_timeout 15000 ms Master services torso_timeout 20000 ms Torso services callback_queue_capacity 256 Bounded callback queue capacity in tasks master_status_max_age 500 ms Maximum receive age for motion admission; must be positive command_channel kUnspecified Set explicitly for single-part sends time_sync Enabled, software mode Prepares gPTP after connection; see Time-sync parameters.

docs.title: Errors and result checking
docs.text:
Check SDK call errors, robot service outcomes and runtime device faults separately:

Layer How to obtain it Handling SDK call result C++: Result<T>.error().code/message or Status.code()/message(); Python: catch NorthSDKError, read .code and the exception text Resolve argument, connection, timeout or SDK motion-gate issues first. Codes are listed below. Robot service result Ordinary response success/message; Master result/message; configuration service result and diagnostics A received response still needs a business-result check. Master success is MasterResult::kOk; configuration success is ConfigResult::kOk. Robot runtime fault Part Client on_heartbeat(): error_code/fault_mask/fault_codes; Master on_error() / on_degradation(): error_code/reason/device_errors Stop sending motion targets and record the subsystem, fault codes and reason. Resolve site causes before reset; contact support for persistent faults.

Interpret device faults using the corresponding device definitions: HandServiceResponse.sdk_error_code comes from the hand device SDK, and PowerCommandResponse.error_code comes from the power service. North SDK call errors use ErrorCode; kRemoteFailure indicates a communication error reply.

ErrorCode Handling kOk Success kInvalidArgument Correct lengths, finite values, enum values, confirmations or configuration kNotConnected Connect successfully before calling kUnavailable Check device service availability and connectivity kTimeout Response wait timed out; inspect results before retrying side effects kSerialization Check matching software versions and retain error details and logs kTransport Retain the Zenoh/network error and inspect connectivity kStaleState Missing, malformed or stale state; wait for fresh state kOutcomeUnknown Master outcome unknown; inspect state without automatic retry kRemoteFailure Zenoh error reply received; inspect message kInternal Retain error details and logs, and contact support kMotionNotAllowed Check Master phase and channel/mode kNotSupported The current version or device does not support the requested operation or parameter; check arguments and version applicability kTimeSyncUnavailable Check host-component installation and the service error message. kTimeSyncPermission Use the authorized account; software mode also needs system-time authorization. kTimeSyncUnsupported Check the selected mode and NIC timestamping capabilities. kTimeSyncConflict Check other time services or conflicting synchronization sessions. kTimeSyncTimeout Check the link and interface, and whether synchronization continues converging. kTimeSyncLost Synchronization is not ready or has been lost; wait for readiness.

After a timeout or error reply, the server may already have performed the operation. Inspect actual state before retrying.

docs.title: Common Python signatures
docs.text:
Apart from the differences below, method names match C++ and enums use uppercase underscores. Subscription options may be omitted, defaulting to SubscribeOptions(). Synchronous services return response objects directly.

Python call Return NorthSDK(config); sdk.connect(); sdk.close() SDK object; the latter two return None on success. sdk.time_sync_diagnostics(); sdk.robot_time_ns() TimeSyncDiagnostics; integer nanoseconds. client.latest_state(max_age_ms=1000) Part state; latest_status/latest_imu/latest_battery also use max_age_ms=1000. client.on_state(callback, options=SubscribeOptions()) Subscription; Master uses on_status. sdk.master().on_heartbeat(subsystem, callback, options=SubscribeOptions()) Subscription. sdk.master().set_mode(mode); start_task(task_id); stop_task(status=0) MasterResponse; check result. sdk.arm(side).send_joint_positions(positions) None; seven positions. The hand method of the same name takes twenty-two. sdk.torso().send_joint_command(command) None; command is a JointCommand. sdk.whole_body().send(channel, command) None; command is a WholeBodyCommand. sdk.video().on_jpeg(source, callback, options=VideoOptions()) Subscription; diagnostics(source) returns VideoDiagnostics. sdk.alignment().on_frame(options, callback, callback_options=SubscribeOptions()) Subscription; diagnostics(subscription) returns AlignmentDiagnostics. sdk.config().get(plugin_id=""); set(plugin_id, operations) ConfigGetResponse / ConfigSetResponse.

Python tolerances are integer ns (max_skew_ns); waits and cache ages are integer ms (such as timeout_ms and wait_timeout_ms). sdk.connected, subscription.active and sample.matched are properties, without parentheses.

docs.title: Public capability scope
docs.text:
The following table summarizes the capabilities of each Client.

Client Public capability Config Instance discovery, descriptors, persistent SET/RESET Master Status, hardware health, events, heartbeat, task and lifecycle services WholeBody Multi-part position/velocity commands and command mirror Chassis State, heartbeat, cache, velocity, Motion/Force mode, enable and reset Torso State, heartbeat, cache, complete positions, enable, reset, mode and action cancel Arm Side-specific state, heartbeat, cache, complete positions, enable, mode, estop, reset and action cancel Hand State, tactile/e-skin, complete positions, modes, tactile/e-skin calibration, zero-calibration query/stop Sensors IMU, ultrasonic, tactile skin, Lidar and tactile-skin zeroing Power Board/battery state, heartbeat, read-only queries and explicitly confirmed power management Video Four AU decoders, JPEG callbacks and diagnostics; requires a video-enabled package and its runtime dependencies Alignment Source-timestamp matching and diagnostics for video, device and Master state

Capabilities depend on installed and enabled robot devices. Check device state, SDK errors and business responses during operation.

docs.title: Client APIs
docs.text: Each on_* returns Result<Subscription>; latest takes a maximum age. Usage rules and API declarations follow. For application workflows see Application Development.

docs.title: NorthSDK
docs.text:
Create and connect an instance, then use accessors to obtain Clients. version() reports the version; connected() reports local connection state.

class NorthSDK {
public:
    static Result<std::unique_ptr<NorthSDK>> Create(const SdkConfig& config);
    ~NorthSDK();
    NorthSDK(const NorthSDK&) = delete;
    NorthSDK& operator=(const NorthSDK&) = delete;

    Status connect();
    void close();
    bool connected() const noexcept;
    CallbackDiagnostics callback_diagnostics() const;
    TimeSyncDiagnostics time_sync_diagnostics() const;
    Result<std::int64_t> robot_time_ns() const;
    static const char* version() noexcept;

    ConfigClient config();
    MasterClient master();
    WholeBodyClient whole_body();
    ChassisClient chassis();
    TorsoClient torso();
    ArmClient arm(Side side);
    HandClient hand(Side side);
    SensorClient sensors();
    PowerClient power();
    VideoClient video();
    AlignmentClient alignment();

};
API Parameters Result and purpose Notes Create(config) config: SdkConfig C++ returns Result<std::unique_ptr<NorthSDK>>; creates without connecting Validates channel, timeouts, and callback capacity. Python uses NorthSDK(config) and raises NorthSDKError on failure. connect() None C++ Status; Python returns None on success Establishes communication and prepares configured synchronization. By default a time-sync error retains communication; check connected and synchronization diagnostics separately. close() None No result Cancels subscriptions, clears caches, and closes connections. Recreate user subscriptions after reconnecting. Destruction and Python with exit also close. connected() None bool Reports whether the local communication session is established. Check heartbeats and state streams for device availability. callback_diagnostics() None CallbackDiagnostics Returns cumulative dropped/coalesced callback counts and the latest decode error. time_sync_diagnostics() None TimeSyncDiagnostics Reads synchronization state, offset and errors; see Time-sync parameters. robot_time_ns() None C++ Result<int64_t>; Python int, in ns Reads a local clock synchronized to North gPTP. Returns an error if disconnected, disabled or not ready. version() None Version string Static; no SDK instance or connection is required. config(), master(), whole_body(), chassis(), torso(), sensors(), power(), video(), alignment() None Corresponding Client Clients cannot communicate after the SDK closes. arm(side), hand(side) side: Side Side-bound Client Left/Right are from the robot's perspective. An invalid value is rejected by later calls.

SdkConfig.connect_endpoints and zenoh_config_path select the target. Single-part motion also requires command_channel before creation. See SdkConfig defaults.

docs.title: Subscription
docs.text:
A move-only subscription handle. Retain it to receive callbacks; destruction or close() cancels it.

class Subscription {
public:
    Subscription();
    ~Subscription();
    Subscription(Subscription&&) noexcept;
    Subscription& operator=(Subscription&&) noexcept;
    Subscription(const Subscription&) = delete;
    Subscription& operator=(const Subscription&) = delete;

    void close();
    bool active() const noexcept;

};
API Parameters Result and purpose Notes close() None Cancels the subscription Call explicitly or rely on C++ destruction; Python may use with subscription:. No new callback starts after it returns. active() None bool Reports whether the handle remains open.

docs.title: ConfigClient
docs.text:
class ConfigClient {
public:
    Result<ConfigGetResponse> get(const std::string& plugin_id = {});
    Result<ConfigSetResponse> set(
        const std::string& plugin_id,
        const std::vector<ConfigFieldOperation>& operations);
};

get() queries robot-exposed configuration instances and fields. set() persists configuration changes. Use instance and field IDs returned by get().

API Parameters and return get(plugin_id="") Empty queries all instances; a non-empty ID queries one instance. Returns ConfigGetResponse. set(plugin_id, operations) Takes an instance and a list of field operations. SET carries a value; RESET does not. Returns ConfigSetResponse.

Require result == ConfigResult::kOk; inspect diagnostics on failure. Before writing, check the field descriptor’s type, range and application conditions. After writing, inspect effective_value and pending_init. After a write timeout, call get() to confirm the actual result.

See Configuration data for types and fields.

docs.title: MasterClient
docs.text:
Provides runtime status, health, task events and system services. Use task IDs configured on the robot. on_heartbeat accepts a subsystem name or *. Check Master response.result, then observe state after transitions.

class MasterClient {
public:
    Result<Subscription> on_status(std::function<void(const MasterStatus&)> callback,
                                   const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<Subscription> on_hardware_health(
        std::function<void(const SystemHardwareHealth&)> callback,
        const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<Subscription> on_task_start(std::function<void(const MasterEvent&)> callback,
                                       const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<Subscription> on_task_stop(std::function<void(const MasterEvent&)> callback,
                                      const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<Subscription> on_degradation(std::function<void(const MasterEvent&)> callback,
                                        const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<Subscription> on_error(std::function<void(const MasterEvent&)> callback,
                                  const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<Subscription> on_heartbeat(const std::string& subsystem,
                                      std::function<void(const Heartbeat&)> callback,
                                      const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<MasterStatus> latest_status(std::chrono::milliseconds max_age);

    Result<MasterResponse> set_mode(OperationMode mode);
    Result<MasterResponse> start_task(const std::string& task_id);
    Result<MasterResponse> stop_task(std::int32_t status = 0);
    Result<MasterResponse> reset();
    Result<MasterResponse> enter_ota();
    Result<MasterResponse> exit_ota();
    Result<MasterResponse> enter_estop();
    Result<MasterResponse> exit_estop();
    Result<ConfigSetResponse> set_health_requirement(const std::string& subsystem,
                                                     HealthRequirement requirement);
    Result<ConfigSetResponse> set_safety_guard_enabled(const std::string& guard_id, bool enabled);
    Result<BasicResponse> prepare_teleoperation();

};
API Parameters Result data Purpose and constraints on_status(callback, options) Common subscription parameters MasterStatus Subscribe to Master phase, operating mode, task ID, and degradation state. on_hardware_health(callback, options) Common subscription parameters SystemHardwareHealth Subscribe to subsystem health, safety guards, and host resource summary. on_task_start(callback, options) Common subscription parameters MasterEvent Subscribe to task-start acceptance, active state, and reason. on_task_stop(callback, options) Common subscription parameters MasterEvent Subscribe to task-stop events and final status. on_degradation(callback, options) Common subscription parameters MasterEvent Subscribe to system degradation events. on_error(callback, options) Common subscription parameters MasterEvent Subscribe to Master errors and per-device error details. on_heartbeat(subsystem, callback, options) subsystem: string and common subscription parameters Heartbeat Subscribe to a subsystem such as "lidar"; use "*" for all. A specific subsystem name must be non-empty and contain no wildcard/path special characters. latest_status(max_age) Maximum local receive age MasterStatus Actively read fresh Master cache; absent or expired data returns kStaleState. set_mode(mode) OperationMode: Teleoperation, Inference or Automation MasterResponse Changes Master operation mode; robot state determines whether switching is allowed. See Application Development for the task preparation sequence. start_task(task_id) Non-empty, case-sensitive task ID, such as inference, teleoperation, home or docking; availability follows the delivery configuration MasterResponse Requests task start. After an accepted response, still wait for streamed RUNNING state. stop_task(status=0) 32-bit task exit status, default 0; other values are task-defined MasterResponse Requests normal task completion. teleoperation quiesces remote control, performs homing and finalizes recording while remaining RUNNING. An accepted response does not mean standstill. Observe status and feedback for other tasks too. Do not use as an emergency stop. reset() None MasterResponse Requests the Master recovery flow; allowed phases and result are decided by the robot state machine. enter_ota() / exit_ota() None MasterResponse Enter or leave OTA phase, affecting tasks and device operations. enter_estop() None MasterResponse Requests system emergency stop; check device feedback to confirm the outcome. exit_estop() None MasterResponse Starts asynchronous recovery: resets and re-enables both arms and torso, and returns both hands to position mode. Success means recovery started. Wait for Master to leave ESTOP and check device health and feedback. Confirm the site is ready first; do not restart the old control loop directly. set_health_requirement(subsystem, requirement) Subsystem ID and HealthRequirement such as OK, WARNING, or OFF ConfigSetResponse Persists Master health admission through Config and returns ConfigSetResponse. set_safety_guard_enabled(guard_id, enabled) Guard ID and enabled flag ConfigSetResponse Persists a safety-guard setting through Config and returns ConfigSetResponse; restrict to authorized management. prepare_teleoperation() None BasicResponse Prepares the teleoperation path in Master Teleoperation mode. Start the teleoperation task once preparation is complete. Check BasicResponse.success/message.

Master services require a connected SDK and use master_timeout (15000 ms by default). C++ checks Result<MasterResponse> followed by result == MasterResult::kOk; Python checks MasterResult.OK on the returned response and raises NorthSDKError on SDK failures. Check BasicResponse.success/message for prepare_teleoperation(). Health-requirement and safety-guard settings persist through Config; check ConfigResult::kOk and diagnostics.

For set_mode, Teleoperation, Inference and Automation correspond to the same-named CommandChannels. Universal skips mode matching only when sending and still requires fresh RUNNING state. before/after are response snapshots and message explains the business result; continue observing on_status or latest_status to confirm actual mode and phase. See Master mode service.

Common SDK errors include kNotConnected, kInvalidArgument, kTimeout, kTransport, kRemoteFailure and kOutcomeUnknown. See Common parameters and results for subscription and cache rules.

docs.title: WholeBodyClient
docs.text:
Combines position targets and chassis velocity commands for multiple parts.

class WholeBodyClient {
public:
    Status send(CommandChannel channel, const WholeBodyCommand& command);
    Result<Subscription> on_command(std::function<void(const WholeBodyCommand&)> callback,
                                    const SubscribeOptions& options = {});

};
API Parameters Result and purpose Constraints send(channel, command) channel: CommandChannel; command: WholeBodyCommand C++ Status; Python returns None on success Channel must be Teleoperation, Inference, Automation, or Universal. Supply at least one part; only populated optionals update. Every part is locally validated. Parts execute separately; check feedback for each part. on_command(callback, options) Common subscription parameters WholeBodyCommand callback Records the combined command mirror; read device state for execution results.

The channel argument of each send() call selects the sending channel. It still requires fresh RUNNING Master state.

docs.title: ChassisClient
docs.text:
Velocity uses m/s and rad/s and must be finite. set_mode explicitly selects overall Motion/Force mode; mode reads current mode from cached chassis heartbeat. Switching requires an idle chassis outside OTA.

class ChassisClient {
public:
    Result<Subscription> on_state(std::function<void(const ChassisState&)> callback,
                                  const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<Subscription> on_heartbeat(std::function<void(const Heartbeat&)> callback,
                                      const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<ChassisState> latest_state(std::chrono::milliseconds max_age);
    Status send_velocity(const ChassisVelocity& command);
    Result<ChassisModeResponse> set_mode(ChassisControlMode mode);
    Result<ChassisControlMode> mode(
        std::chrono::milliseconds max_age = std::chrono::milliseconds(500));
    Result<BasicResponse> enable(bool enabled = true);
    Result<BasicResponse> reset();

};
API Parameters Result data Purpose and constraints on_state(callback, options) Common subscription parameters ChassisState Subscribe to chassis velocity, joint, electrical, and mode state. on_heartbeat(callback, options) Common subscription parameters Heartbeat Subscribe to lifecycle, online masks, faults, and rates. latest_state(max_age) Maximum local receive age; Python default 1000 ms ChassisState Missing or expired data returns kStaleState. send_velocity(command) ChassisVelocity Status / Python None vx, vy, and extension_velocity are m/s; vtheta is rad/s. All values must be finite. Uses the single-part command channel and Master gate. set_mode(mode) ChassisControlMode::kMotion / kForce ChassisModeResponse Switches overall motion/force mode and returns success/message, previous_mode, and current_mode. After switching, confirm the device is enabled. mode(max_age=500ms) Maximum local heartbeat age ChassisControlMode Reads fresh cached heartbeat without a service request. First call or expired heartbeat returns kStaleState; Python uses max_age_ms. enable(enabled=true) enabled: bool BasicResponse Requests enable or disable; inspect business response and subsequent state. reset() None BasicResponse Requests chassis reset; determine enable/mode changes from device feedback.

Mode switching requires an idle chassis outside OTA freeze. Heartbeat period may exceed the default 500 ms window, so applications may choose a larger age while still handling stale results. Velocity commands do not apply authoritative model limits in the SDK; use delivered limits. For normal stopping, keep sending zero velocity and use fresh ChassisState.velocity to require translation and rotation within application-defined rest tolerances for the required duration.

docs.title: TorsoClient
docs.text:
Eight joints are ordered body J1–J5 then neck J6–J8. Send complete positions. Reset leaves joints disabled; enable through the application workflow before motion. Services use torso_timeout.

Array indices start at zero: for example, J6 is position[5]. The figure shows array order; joint positions are in rad.

class TorsoClient {
public:
    Result<Subscription> on_state(std::function<void(const TorsoState&)> callback,
                                  const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<Subscription> on_heartbeat(std::function<void(const Heartbeat&)> callback,
                                      const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<TorsoState> latest_state(std::chrono::milliseconds max_age);
    Status send_joint_command(const JointCommand& command);
    Result<BasicResponse> enable(bool enabled = true);
    Result<BasicResponse> reset();
    Result<ModeResponse> set_mode(TorsoControlMode mode);
    Result<ModeResponse> set_mode(std::uint32_t mode);
    Result<BasicResponse> cancel_waypoints();

};
API Parameters Result data Purpose and constraints on_state(callback, options) Common subscription parameters TorsoState Subscribe to eight-joint state and electrical data. on_heartbeat(callback, options) Common subscription parameters Heartbeat Subscribe to torso health and rates. latest_state(max_age) Maximum local receive age; Python default 1000 ms TorsoState Missing or expired data returns kStaleState. send_joint_command(command) JointCommand Status / Python None Supports exactly eight position values in rad; name, velocity, and torque must be empty. Uses the single-part channel and Master gate. enable(enabled=true) bool BasicResponse Requests enable/disable and uses torso_timeout. reset() None BasicResponse Requests reset. The current contract leaves joints disabled after reset; explicitly re-enable before motion. set_mode(mode) Prefer TorsoControlMode; a uint32_t overload remains ModeResponse Switches Position/MIT device mode; check success, previous_mode, and current_mode. cancel_waypoints() None BasicResponse Requests waypoint cancellation; continue reading state to confirm the outcome.

All torso services use SdkConfig.torso_timeout, 20000 ms by default.

docs.title: ArmClient
docs.text:
arm(Side) selects an arm with seven joints. Mode, enable, estop and reset are explicit services. Check business results and device state after mode changes.

class ArmClient {
public:
    Side side() const noexcept;
    Result<Subscription> on_state(std::function<void(const ArmState&)> callback,
                                  const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<Subscription> on_heartbeat(std::function<void(const Heartbeat&)> callback,
                                      const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<ArmState> latest_state(std::chrono::milliseconds max_age);
    Status send_joint_positions(const std::array<float, 7>& positions);
    Status send_joint_command(const JointCommand& command);
    Result<BasicResponse> enable(bool enabled = true);
    Result<ModeResponse> set_mode(ControlMode mode);
    Result<BasicResponse> estop(const std::string& reason = {});
    Result<BasicResponse> reset();
    Result<BasicResponse> cancel_waypoints();

};

Select the arm through sdk.arm(Side); side() returns the Client’s bound side.

API Parameters Result data Purpose and constraints side() None Side Returns the side bound when the Client was created. on_state(callback, options) Common subscription parameters; default DropOldest ArmState callback Receive this arm’s state for feedback, monitoring or recording; retain the subscription. on_heartbeat(callback, options) Common subscription parameters Heartbeat Subscribe to lifecycle, joint online masks, faults, and rates for this arm. latest_state(max_age) Required C++ milliseconds; Python max_age_ms=1000, nonnegative ArmState Returns a copy subject to local receive age and automatically establishes reception; missing/expired samples return kStaleState. send_joint_positions(positions) C++ std::array<float, 7>; Python numeric sequence of length 7, finite values in rad Status / Python None Submits a complete target for this arm in model-defined joint order; no name reordering, sparse updates, velocity or torque control. send_joint_command(command) JointCommand Status / Python None Same constraints as send_joint_positions: exactly seven positions; name, velocity, and torque must be empty. enable(enabled=true) bool BasicResponse Requests enable/disable; check success/message and observe state. set_mode(mode) ControlMode ModeResponse Requests a device control mode. Position commands require the compatible mode defined by the robot procedure. Master OperationMode is a separate concept. estop(reason="") Optional reason string BasicResponse Requests an emergency stop for this arm. reason records the emergency-stop cause. reset() None BasicResponse Requests reset; reconfirm mode, enable state, heartbeat, and state afterward. cancel_waypoints() None BasicResponse Requests cancellation of an arm waypoint task; observe feedback to confirm.

See Common parameters and results for subscription and cache rules.

Position sending requires SdkConfig.command_channel set at creation, a connected SDK, Master RUNNING no older than master_status_max_age, matching Teleoperation/Inference/Automation channel and Master mode, and an enabled device in a compatible position mode. The SDK validates length, finite values and motion admission. See Motion control for target preparation.

Common send errors are kInvalidArgument, kNotConnected, kStaleState, kMotionNotAllowed and kTransport. Compare fresh ArmState.joints.position against the target using application tolerance and timeout. Stop sending on stale feedback, Master leaving RUNNING or errors. See Send a single-arm target.

Ordinary Arm services use service_timeout, 6000 ms by default. Use subsequent state to confirm mode, enable, reset and estop outcomes.

docs.title: HandClient
docs.text:
Each hand has twenty-two joints. Tactile finger channels 0–4 run from little finger to thumb, with kRaw/kDeform images. Python image payloads are bytes. Tactile calibration accepts enabled=true only. Zero-calibration status query and stop are available. Check success/message.

Select the hand with hand(Side), then select the finger. Both hands use 0=little, 1=ring, 2=middle, 3=index, 4=thumb. finger=4 selects the thumb of the selected hand.

class HandClient {
public:
    Side side() const noexcept;
    Result<Subscription> on_state(std::function<void(const HandState&)> callback,
                                  const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<Subscription> on_heartbeat(std::function<void(const Heartbeat&)> callback,
                                      const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<Subscription> on_tactile_force(std::uint32_t finger,
                                          std::function<void(const TactileForce&)> callback,
                                          const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<Subscription> on_tactile_image(std::uint32_t finger, TactileImageKind kind,
                                          std::function<void(const CompressedImage&)> callback,
                                          const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<Subscription> on_eskin_force(std::function<void(const HandEskinForce&)> callback,
                                        const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<Subscription> on_eskin_raw(std::function<void(const HandEskinRaw&)> callback,
                                      const SubscribeOptions& options = {});
    Result<HandState> latest_state(std::chrono::milliseconds max_age);
    Status send_joint_positions(const std::array<float, 22>& positions);
    Status send_joint_command(const JointCommand& command);
    Result<HandServiceResponse> set_mode(HandMode mode);
    Result<HandServiceResponse> set_mode(std::uint32_t mode);
    Result<HandServiceResponse> calibrate_tactile(bool enabled = true);
    Result<HandServiceResponse> calibrate_eskin();
    Result<HandServiceResponse> zero_calibration_status();
    Result<HandServiceResponse> stop_zero_calibration();

};

Select the side with sdk.hand(Side). All services use service_timeout. For HandServiceResponse, inspect success/message and, when relevant, result, mode, calibration state, and progress fields.

API Parameters Callback/result Purpose and constraints side() None Side Returns the bound hand side. on_state(callback, options) Common subscription parameters HandState Subscribe to 22-joint, electrical, and force information. on_heartbeat(callback, options) Common subscription parameters Heartbeat Subscribe to hand health and rates. on_tactile_force(finger, callback, options) finger 0–4 TactileForce Subscribe to six-axis tactile force; 0=little finger and 4=thumb. docs.text:
Provides IMU, ultrasonic, tactile skin and Lidar data. The SDK automatically decompresses Zstd Lidar data into points; no additional decompression library is required. public:

Angular velocity is rad/s, linear acceleration is m/s², and quaternion fields are w/x/y/z. on_ultrasonic(callback, options) Common subscription parameters UltrasonicSamples Subscribe to ultrasonic distance/status. docs.text:

    Result<BatterySystemState> latest_battery(std::chrono::milliseconds max_age);
    Result<PowerCommandResponse> channel_command(const PowerChannelCommand& command);
    Result<PowerCommandResponse> estop(PowerNode node, const std::string& reason);
    Result<PowerCommandResponse> release_estop(PowerNode node, const std::string& reason,
                                               bool confirm_power_change);

Read-only operations need no confirmation; state-changing opcodes require confirm_power_change=true. estop(node, reason) PowerNode and reason PowerCommandResponse Request emergency stop for a power node. Supply a traceable reason and check success, error_code, and later state. release_estop(node, reason, confirm_power_change=false) Node, non-empty reason, explicit confirmation PowerCommandResponse Releasing estop changes power state. Pass true; the default false prevents accidental calls. shutdown(node, reason, confirm_power_change=false) Node, non-empty reason, explicit confirmation PowerCommandResponse Shut down a node. Explicit confirmation is mandatory and connection/state streams may stop immediately.

In PowerChannelCommand, channel_id/action apply to channel operations, set_mask/clear_mask to mask operations, and heartbeat_period_ms to the corresponding heartbeat-period command; the selected PowerOpCode determines the valid combination. Power services use service_timeout; after timeout, inspect remaining telemetry or the physical system before retrying.

docs.text:
class VideoClient {
public:
    Result<Subscription> on_jpeg(
        VideoSource source,
        std::function<void(const JpegFrame&)> callback,
        const VideoOptions& options = {});
    Result<VideoDiagnostics> diagnostics(VideoSource source) const;
};

Subscribe to camera JPEG images and inspect reception diagnostics. Video runtime dependencies are bundled; complete Video environment setup before use.

Method Parameters Return Notes on_jpeg(source, callback, options) source: head left/right H.265 or wrist left/right H.264; callback: receives JpegFrame; options: VideoOptions Result<Subscription> Retain the handle. Each camera permits one active subscription, including use by alignment sessions. diagnostics(source) The subscribed VideoSource Result<VideoDiagnostics> Inspect received/output counts, drops, resets and the latest error.

VideoOptions defaults to NVDEC, JPEG quality 85 and 1280×960 output. Configure decoder_backend, jpeg_quality, output_width/output_height and input queue capacities. Both dimensions set to 0 preserve source size. Select kSoftware explicitly for software decoding; there is no automatic fallback, and multi-stream or high-resolution performance is limited.

JpegFrame contains the source, header, dimensions and complete JPEG data. C++ references are valid only during the callback; copy for asynchronous use. Python data is bytes. Keep callbacks short; slow consumers may skip frames.

Invalid parameters return kInvalidArgument; an occupied camera returns kUnavailable. Inspect returned errors and diagnostics() for video environment failures.

docs.text:
class AlignmentClient {
public:

        const AlignmentOptions& options,
        std::function<void(const AlignedFrame&)> callback,
        const SubscribeOptions& callback_options = {});
    Result<AlignmentDiagnostics> diagnostics(
        const Subscription& subscription) const;
};

Matches samples from multiple sources using timestamps in the same clock domain.

Method Parameters Return Notes on_frame(options, callback, callback_options) options: AlignmentOptions; callback: receives AlignedFrame Result<Subscription> Retain the handle. callback_options currently does not affect output behavior. Keep callbacks short. diagnostics(subscription) An active alignment subscription belonging to this SDK Result<AlignmentDiagnostics> Inspect complete/incomplete frames, timestamp anomalies and per-source matching counts. AlignmentOptions Description baseline / sources Baseline and additional sources. Head-left is the default baseline and automatically includes head-right. Other baselines match only explicit sources. Sources must not repeat. max_skew / per-source max_skew Matching tolerance; per-source settings take precedence. 0 requires identical timestamps. Unset values use the defaults below. Per-source direction Default kAtOrBefore selects data no later than the baseline. Alternatives are kNearest and kAtOrAfter. wait_timeout Alignment waiting time, default 20 ms. buffer_capacity / emit_incomplete Default per-source capacity 64; incomplete frames are emitted by default. video_options Shared VideoOptions for video sources, which occupy camera subscriptions.

Default tolerances: arm/torso/chassis/hand joints/IMU 7.5 ms, eskin 15 ms, video 25 ms, finger tactile 50 ms, Master 150 ms. Python tolerance and wait attributes are max_skew_ns and wait_timeout_ms; None uses default tolerance.

AlignedFrame contains timestamp_ns, baseline_sample, samples in sources order, and complete. Status is Matched, Missing or OutOfTolerance. See Video and alignment data for reading results. offset_ns is the candidate timestamp minus the baseline timestamp.

Head JPEG uses RK SEI source time; other devices usually use Header time. Confirm a common clock domain before cross-source alignment. See Example Code Reference for usage.

docs.title: Time-sync parameters
docs.text:
SdkConfig.time_sync uses the fields below. Software mode adjusts host system time; see Time synchronization for host setup.

TimeSyncOptions field Default and constraints enabled true; disable to skip synchronization. mode TimeSyncMode::kSoftware; alternatively kHardware. Python: TimeSyncMode.SOFTWARE/HARDWARE. interface Empty; select the physical wired NIC from the robot endpoint route. Ambiguous selection is an error. timeout / Python timeout_ms 60000 ms, strictly positive; initial synchronization preparation deadline. failure_policy TimeSyncFailurePolicy::kKeepConnected: initial synchronization error retains communication. kFailConnection closes communication. Python: KEEP_CONNECTED/FAIL_CONNECTION. software_offset_threshold_ns 1000000 ns; range 1–1000000000 ns, for software readiness only. Hardware mode uses a fixed 50 ns threshold.

TimeSyncDiagnostics.state is Disabled, Preparing, Ready, Failed or Lost (C++ enum names have a k prefix; Python uses uppercase underscores). Readiness requires ten consecutive new observations with absolute offset below the threshold. Check again after synchronization loss during operation.

Diagnostic field Meaning error SDK error code and message. mode/interface/phc_device Selected mode, NIC and hardware clock device; software mode has no PHC device. clock_source/system_time_owned Clock source, CLOCK_REALTIME or PHC, and whether this component manages system-time synchronization. offset_ns/offset_threshold_ns Observed offset and readiness threshold in ns; the threshold determines synchronization readiness. stable_samples/required_samples Consecutive acceptable observations and required count. sample_age / Python sample_age_ms Diagnostic sample age; over one second is no longer ready.

docs.title: Data types and fields
docs.text: The excerpts below cover public types and fields used by the documented APIs, and result-reading methods. Refer to the delivered public headers for declarations. Plan command targets in the application. Inspect quality, heartbeat and freshness before using state data.

docs.title: Common field meanings
docs.text: Field Units and reading rules JointState / JointElectricalState Equal indices identify the same joint. See Joint arrays and coordinates. Read valid fields within the actual array lengths. ChassisVelocity / ChassisState.velocity Body +x forward, +y left; positive yaw is counterclockwise viewed from above. vx/vy are m/s and vtheta is rad/s. Feedback is velocity.linear.x/y and velocity.angular.z. Header.stamp_ns Source time; 0 means unavailable. latest_* ages data from local reception. Header.frame_id / Pose / Wrench / LidarPoint frame_id identifies a source or coordinate frame. Points are in m, forces in N and torques in Nm. Apply the delivered coordinate definitions before combining devices. ImuSamples.imus Each entry is one IMU, with rad/s angular velocity and m/s² linear acceleration. Identify sources by their Headers and use the mounting definition when interpreting orientation. HandState.force_info Raw integer force-sensor information from the device. Use on_tactile_force() for fingertip six-axis forces. Heartbeat / MasterDeviceError Heartbeat expected_mask/online_mask/fault_mask are device bitmasks. In both types, fault_codes are device fault codes. Retain the subsystem and error message for diagnosis. BatteryPack Pack and cell voltages in V, current in A, soc/soh in percent (0–100), power limits in W and temperatures in °C. Check quality/value per PowerReading. PowerBoardState.readings Read by name and unit. Absent outputs[].enabled means unknown. PowerSampleMetadata clock_domain identifies the power sample’s clock domain; confirm a common clock domain before comparing timestamps.

docs.title: Configuration data
docs.text:
Type or field Meaning ConfigGetResponse / ConfigSetResponse result is the business outcome and diagnostics explains it. Queries return instances; writes return an optional instance. ConfigInstanceInfo / ConfigFieldInfo plugin_id identifies the instance, field_id the field, and field_descriptor its type, unit, constraints and safety conditions. ConfigFieldOperation field_id, operation and optional value. ConfigValue supports bool, int64, finite double, string, double array and int64 array. Python constructors are boolean/integer/real/string/double_array/integer_array(). effective_value / saved_override Current effective value and saved override; either may be absent. apply_policy / pending_init Application policy is IMMEDIATE, SAFE_STATE or INIT_ONLY. pending_init indicates a change awaiting initialization. ConfigDiagnostic code/field_id/message identify the problem; optional element_index identifies an array element.

On RecoveryRequired, restore device state before changing configuration.

docs.title: Video and alignment data
docs.text:
Type Essential fields and rules VideoSource kHeadLeft/kHeadRight/kWristLeft/kWristRight; Python: HEAD_LEFT/HEAD_RIGHT/WRIST_LEFT/WRIST_RIGHT. VideoOptions jpeg_quality defaults to 85 (1–100); decoder_backend defaults to NVDEC. Default dimensions are 1280×960; both zero preserve input size. max_pending_frames defaults to 32 (1–4096), max_pending_bytes to 16 MiB, and max_au_bytes to 4 MiB (positive, at most 64 MiB and no larger than max_pending_bytes). Width and height must not exceed 8192. JpegFrame source/header/width/height/data describe a complete JPEG. Optional source_timestamp_ns requires checking timestamp_status (Valid/Missing/Invalid/NotApplicable). sdk_latency_ns covers input reception to C++ callback entry; pipeline_latency_ns covers processing inside the decoder pipeline. Neither includes browser display or Python GIL wait. VideoDiagnostics active/waiting_for_keyframe, received_au_count/jpeg_frame_count, drop/reset counters and last_error distinguish no input, waiting for a keyframe and decode failure. AlignmentSource kind selects the type. Arms/hands use side; tactile sources also use finger/tactile_image_kind; video uses video_source. Match controls are direction and optional max_skew; Python tolerance is max_skew_ns. AlignmentDataKind Supports ChassisState, TorsoState, ArmState, HandState, TactileForce, TactileImage, HandEskinForce, HandEskinRaw, ImuSamples, TactileSkinSamples, VideoJpeg and MasterStatus. C++ uses a k prefix; Python uses uppercase underscores. AlignedSample source/status/timestamp_ns/offset_ns/value. When matched() (Python property matched) is true, read the matched result with C++ get<T>() or Python value. AlignedFrame timestamp_ns/baseline_sample are the baseline time and data. samples follows explicit sources order. complete means all required sources matched. Default stereo also exposes left/right results through left_image/right_sample. AlignmentDiagnostics Frame counts: evaluated_frame_count/emitted_frame_count/incomplete_frame_count. Per-source baseline/sources expose received_count/matched_count/missing_count/out_of_tolerance_count to diagnose missing input or tolerance failures. invalid_timestamp_count/regression_count identify invalid or regressing time.

Before computing data latency from robot_time_ns(), confirm that the source uses the same gPTP domain. For head video, use source_timestamp_ns with a valid timestamp_status.

docs.title: Packages and runtime environment
docs.text:
The package contains C++ headers and shared libraries, Python bindings, examples, and video runtime dependencies. This manual recommends the following development environment.

Development system Recommended Python interpreter C++ API Ubuntu 22.04 LTS x86_64 CPython 3.10.x C++17 Ubuntu 24.04 LTS x86_64 CPython 3.12.x C++17

Other Linux x86_64 environments must meet the minimum runtime symbol requirements recorded in the package BUILD-MANIFEST.json. Compatibility requires validation in the target environment.

The development environment provides the Python interpreter. Its minor version and architecture must match a binding included in the package, as listed in the package manifest. This also applies to virtual environments. Python is unnecessary for C++-only applications.

Extract the entire package into a dedicated directory and preserve its structure. GStreamer runtime libraries and required video plugins are bundled; installing system GStreamer is unnecessary. NVIDIA drivers are not bundled; see Video environment setup.

Directory or file Purpose include/north_sdk/ Public C++ headers lib/ SDK and supporting runtime libraries lib/python/ Bindings for the target Python version lib/video-runtime/ Bundled video libraries, plugins and tools bin/ C++ bring-up and connection diagnostic programs examples/python/ Python examples and environment check script manual/ User manual setup.bash Load this package's library, Python and video plugin paths BUILD-MANIFEST.json Build information, Python ABI and dependencies

To update, replace the complete package, reload its environment and recheck import, read-only connection and state reception.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
This section connects to the robot and receives the first state stream with the fewest steps, without sending motion, mode, calibration or power commands.

Safety: On a first connection, run only the read-only programs in this section. Do not call send_*(), set_mode(), enable(), reset(), calibration or Power management APIs.

docs.title: 1. Connect the robot
docs.text:
Connect the development computer to the Ethernet port led out from the switch on the robot’s rear right side. Power on the robot and wait for its software to start. State communication and time synchronization both use this wired connection.

The default robot IP is 192.168.100.100; the SDK communicates over UDP port 7449. For a direct connection, open Ubuntu Settings → Network → Wired → IPv4 and select Manual. For example, set the computer to 192.168.100.10 with netmask 255.255.255.0, leaving gateway and DNS blank. Check that the address is unused. Use the actual subnet if changed at delivery.

docs.title: 2. Set the SDK and robot address
docs.text:
Replace the SDK path below with your extraction directory. Use the default robot address unless changed for your delivery.

export NORTHSDK_PREFIX=/absolute/path/to/north-sdk
export NORTHSDK_ENDPOINT=udp/192.168.100.100:7449
source "$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/setup.bash"

Environment variables apply only to this terminal and its child processes; configure new terminals separately.

NORTHSDK_PREFIX points to the extracted SDK root containing setup.bash.

Before first use of automatic time synchronization, run this one-time host setup from the ordinary development account:

sudo "$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/tools/setup-host" --user "$USER"
"$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/tools/setup-host" check

This installs the host time-sync component and authorizes the current account. Applications subsequently run without sudo; repeat setup from the new package after an SDK update. Software synchronization may step system time and temporarily pause system time services. Their previous service state is restored after the last time-sync session closes. See Time synchronization to disable it.

docs.title: 3. Run the read-only diagnostic
docs.text:
"$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/bin/north_sdk_robot_smoke" \
  --endpoint "$NORTHSDK_ENDPOINT" --seconds 5

When the basic connection is healthy, the final line is:

PASS

PASS means Master status, hardware health and at least one heartbeat were received. Check each required device stream against the actual configuration; silent means no sample was received for that stream.

docs.title: 4. Receive left-arm state
docs.text:
"$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/bin/north_sdk_quickstart" "$NORTHSDK_ENDPOINT"

When the left arm is online and publishing, output resembles:

left arm seq=1234 joints=7

Press Ctrl+C to exit. If the robot has no left arm, use streams for devices actually installed as reported by robot_smoke.

docs.title: Python users
docs.text:
Run python3 --version and check that the interpreter minor version matches an included binding. CPython 3.10.x on Ubuntu 22.04 and CPython 3.12.x on Ubuntu 24.04 are recommended; virtual environments must also use an interpreter minor version supported by the package.

Step 2 already sets the Python module path. Run the example directly:

python3 "$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/examples/python/quickstart.py" \
  --endpoint "$NORTHSDK_ENDPOINT"

docs.title: Build the C++ example (optional)
docs.text:
After the prebuilt program succeeds, verify the C++ development environment with one g++ command:

g++ -std=c++17 "$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/examples/cpp/quickstart.cpp" \
  -I"$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/include" -L"$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/lib" -lnorth_sdk \
  -Wl,-rpath,"$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/lib" \
  -o north_sdk_quickstart

./north_sdk_quickstart "$NORTHSDK_ENDPOINT"

-L locates link libraries and -Wl,-rpath records the SDK library directory. Still load setup.bash before running to select bundled video libraries and plugins. Rebuild or update the runtime path if the SDK directory moves.

docs.title: Completion criteria
docs.text:
The read-only bring-up is complete when:

  • robot_smoke reports PASS;
  • streams required by the application continuously receive samples;
  • the C++ or Python example exits cleanly;

Continue with the subscription and motion guidance below, then choose task examples in Example Code Reference. If bring-up fails, see First-run troubleshooting below.

docs.title: First-run troubleshooting
docs.text: For first-connection, startup or Python import failures, check the package, shared libraries and network in that order. These checks reuse the environment from step 2 and are needed only on failure.

docs.title: Package or version
docs.text:
test -f "$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/include/north_sdk/NorthSDK.h"
test -f "$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/lib/libnorth_sdk.so"
cat "$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/Version"

Python import check:

python3 -c "import north_sdk; print(north_sdk.NorthSDK.version())"

If you see No module named 'north_sdk._north_sdk', check that the extension exists and matches your Python version:

python3 --version
ls "$NORTHSDK_PREFIX"/lib/python/north_sdk/_north_sdk*.so

Check the package manifest and extensions provided in lib/python/north_sdk/. A cpython-312 filename tag requires CPython 3.12. Switch to a matching interpreter or obtain a package containing the required binding. Replace the package if an extension listed in its manifest is missing.

docs.title: Shared libraries
docs.text:
ldd "$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/bin/north_sdk_quickstart" | \
  grep -E 'north_sdk|zenoh|protobuf|not found'

North SDK, Zenoh and Protobuf should come from one package. If a library is not found or resolves to another SDK/ROS environment, fix LD_LIBRARY_PATH.

docs.title: Network
docs.text:
ip route get 192.168.100.100

Replace the IP with the actual robot address and verify the intended interface. Use ping only when ICMP is permitted. A failed ping does not necessarily mean Zenoh is unavailable; robot_smoke is authoritative.

docs.title: Time synchronization
docs.text:
The SDK prepares gPTP synchronization after establishing communication. Complete the host setup before first use.

Option Usage Software mode (default) Adjusts host system time. The NIC must support software transmit/receive timestamps. Hardware mode Before SDK creation, set config.time_sync.mode to TimeSyncMode::kHardware (C++) or TimeSyncMode.HARDWARE (Python). Requires hardware timestamps and a NIC PHC; adjusts only the NIC clock. Disable Set config.time_sync.enabled = false (C++) or False (Python) before SDK creation.

Check synchronization with:

python3 "$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/examples/python/time_sync_status.py" \
  --endpoint "$NORTHSDK_ENDPOINT" --mode software --seconds 10

When state is READY and robot_time_ns is present, use sdk.robot_time_ns() to read synchronized time. Robot time uses the gPTP domain and is not guaranteed to match UTC.

By default, a synchronization failure makes connect() return an error while retaining communication. Inspect time_sync_diagnostics() for the cause; the status script shows how to handle the error and continue using the connection. If synchronization is lost during operation, wait for readiness before resuming calculations that depend on synchronized time.

For communication-only checks, add --no-time-sync to north_sdk_robot_smoke. See Time-sync parameters for configuration and diagnostic fields.

docs.title: Video environment setup
docs.text: Complete this section when using video. First load the package environment as described in Quick Start. GStreamer runtime libraries, parsing/conversion/JPEG plugins, NVIDIA decoder plugins and a minimal H.264/H.265 software decoder are bundled; installing system GStreamer is unnecessary.

docs.title: NVIDIA drivers and bundled runtime
docs.text:
NVIDIA NVDEC is the default backend. The discrete GPU must support the camera's H.264/H.265 coding profile, with NVIDIA driver and decode libraries matched to the GPU and Ubuntu release. Install NVIDIA drivers separately.

Check the driver first:

nvidia-smi -L

If no GPU is listed, follow the Ubuntu driver installation instructions to install or repair the driver. NVDEC uses driver-provided libcuda.so.1 and libnvcuvid.so.1. See NVIDIA's decode support matrix for supported input profiles.

setup.bash sets SDK video library, plugin and cache paths. Load it in each terminal or application launch environment, and use the current SDK’s runtime and plugins. If the application already loads another GStreamer runtime, receive video in a separate process.

The bundled software decoder supports compatibility and functional debugging. Select it explicitly when no NVIDIA GPU is available; it requires no NVIDIA driver. Software decoding has poor performance for multiple or high-resolution streams and may cause severe frame drops and latency, so it is not recommended for real-time tasks. The SDK never automatically falls back from hardware to software decoding.

docs.title: Check the video environment
docs.text:
Run in the same terminal as the video example. The default recommended backend is NVIDIA hardware decoding:

python3 "$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/examples/python/check_video_env.py" --backend nvdec

The script checks local SDK loading, GStreamer, video plugins and GPU/driver dependencies; C++ users can run it too. All checks reporting OK and a final PASS mean dependencies are available. Receive video next to verify decoding. On FAIL, check the current package environment, library/plugin completeness and driver status.

To check software decoding, pass --backend software to the script. Select the capture or preview program’s decoder separately, as shown next and in Example Code Reference.

docs.title: Receive the first video stream
docs.text:
After the dependency check passes and the robot head-left camera is online, run a single read-only capture for five seconds without saving images:

"$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/bin/north_sdk_video_jpeg" \
  "$NORTHSDK_ENDPOINT" --no-save 0 85 --seconds=5 --nvdec

0 selects head-left and 85 is JPEG quality. At completion, check that JPEG count is greater than zero and no subscription/decoder errors occurred. If no JPEG arrives, check camera publication, network and decoder requirements. For software decoding, replace --nvdec with --software after passing the corresponding environment check.

For browser preview, use the scripts in Example Code Reference. See VideoClient for parameters, sources and diagnostics.

docs.title: Subscriptions and caches
docs.text:
Retain the Subscription returned by on_*(). Destruction or close() cancels it. C++ callback arguments are borrowed references; copy data needed after the callback. Keep callbacks short and move expensive or blocking work to application workers.

latest_*(max_age) returns a local cached copy, aged from local reception. The first call may have no sample or return kStaleState. Wait for a new sample.

Callback policy Purpose kDropOldest Default; discard the oldest droppable callback when full kLatestOnly Coalesce pending samples per subscription for state display kReliable Apply backpressure instead of local dropping

This example uses max_age=500 ms; 250 ms and 700 ms are local receive ages. latest_* establishes the required state reception without a prior on_* call. A separate on_* subscription also receives callbacks.

docs.title: Service results
docs.text: Check the SDK call result first, then the robot service's business result. Monitor heartbeats and error events during operation. C++ uses Result<T> / Status; Python raises NorthSDKError. See Errors and result checking for fields and handling.

docs.title: Motion control
docs.text:
Real motion is not a first-connection test. SDK validation and the Master gate do not replace a hardware emergency stop, model-specific limits, site risk assessment or the robot-side safety controller.

Before the first motion command, complete at least these checks:

  • the emergency stop has been verified and is immediately reachable; the work area is clear and the robot is restrained or supported as required by its model;
  • the joint names, array order, positive directions, zero positions, hard/soft limits and recommended velocity/acceleration for this exact model are available;
  • fresh feedback is read first and a small target is generated from the current position within model limits;
  • the task ID, CommandChannel, Master mode, device enable state and control mode are a supported combination in the delivered robot configuration;
  • the control loop stops sending immediately when feedback becomes stale, Master leaves RUNNING, or an SDK/business error occurs;
  • reviewed task-stop, emergency-stop and recovery procedures are ready, and the on-site supervisor approves the test.

See Motion protection and trajectory processing for robot-side protection, numeric limits and interpolation settings.

Motion commands require fresh RUNNING Master status. Channel-to-mode mapping is below; follow Prepare and end a task for setup.

Channel Master mode kTeleoperation kTeleoperation kInference kInference kAutomation kAutomation kUniversal Any mode; fresh RUNNING is still required

Each arm has seven joints, each hand twenty-two, and the torso eight. Positions are in rad, in fixed device order. Populate complete JointCommand.position only; leave name, velocity and torque empty. A successful send means submission succeeded; determine completion from fresh device feedback.

This sequence illustrates a single-arm position command. Invalid runtime conditions or targets return an SDK error. kUniversal skips mode matching but still requires fresh RUNNING.

docs.title: Prepare and end a task
docs.text:
The following example sends position targets with the inference task.

  1. Configure the channel. Before SDK creation, set config.command_channel = north::CommandChannel::kInference (C++) or config.command_channel = CommandChannel.INFERENCE (Python). WholeBody takes its channel on each send().

  2. Check idle state. Read fresh Master status and require STANDBY. Check required device health and confirm other controllers have stopped sending commands. End any existing task using its own procedure first.

  3. Prepare devices. Call master().set_mode() with OperationMode::kInference / OperationMode.INFERENCE. For each controlled arm select ControlMode::kJointPosition / ControlMode.JOINT_POSITION and call enable(). For torso select TorsoControlMode::kPosition / TorsoControlMode.POSITION and enable it. For hands select HandMode::kPosition / HandMode.POSITION. Check each service result and device feedback.

  4. Start the task. Call master().start_task("inference"), check MasterResult, then wait for streamed status with RUNNING, Inference and task_id == "inference". Resolve device health failures before proceeding.

  5. Send targets. Generate complete, small, continuous targets from fresh position feedback. Continue checking task ID, Master phase/mode and device feedback. Use the joint ordering in the next section.

  6. End normally. Stop the control loop. For chassis, keep sending zero velocity until feedback confirms rest. Call master().stop_task(), check its business result, wait for status to leave RUNNING and check device feedback before closing the SDK. On feedback or communication failure, use the site stopping procedure.

start_task(task_id) takes a case-sensitive task ID. Customer tasks in the standard configuration are listed below; availability follows the delivered configuration. Unconfigured IDs are rejected.

Task ID Purpose inference Inference control; used in this example. teleoperation Teleoperation, with its own preparation flow. home Homing; actively moves the robot. docking Docking.

Normal teleoperation completion performs homing and leaves RUNNING after homing and recording finalization. Stopping teleoperation may cause further motion and must not be used as an emergency stop.

master().exit_estop() starts actuator reset and re-enable, including both arms, torso and hand mode recovery. Clear outgoing motion commands and confirm the site is ready before calling it. A successful response means recovery has started. Wait for Master to leave ESTOP, then check health, control modes and fresh position feedback before starting a new control loop.

docs.title: Joint arrays and coordinates
docs.text:
joints.name[i] and joints.position[i] refer to the same axis. Commands use the same fixed index, with name left empty. Print the complete device state and compare it with the joint definition for the delivered model.

Part Array indices State names Mapping Each arm 0–6 joint_0–joint_6 J1–J7; Side selects left or right. Torso 0–4 torso_0–torso_4 Body J1–J5; J3/J4 are waist pitch/roll joints. Neck 5–7 torso_5–torso_7 Neck J6–J8, sent with the body as a complete eight-position command. Each hand 0–21 joint_0–joint_21 Twenty-two joints.

Positions are in rad. Use the delivered model’s joint definitions for each side’s zero positions, positive axes and hand joint groups.

docs.title: Motion protection and trajectory processing
docs.text: The robot applies command-step checks, limits and interpolation to motion targets. Joint numbers start at 1; SDK indices start at 0.

docs.title: Command admission and fault protection
docs.text:
Arms and torso process streamed position commands using the difference between the new target and the previous accepted target. A frame within every direct-admission threshold is accepted when no catch-up or recovery is pending. Larger steps have their increments limited; steps above Hold reject the entire frame. Axes meeting the fresh-feedback condition below may be exempted from triggering Hold.

Part and checking space Direct-admission threshold Hold threshold Catch-up rate Each arm, joint angles J1–J7 0.1745 rad per joint J1–J4: 0.3491 rad; J5–J7: 0.5236 rad J1–J7: 2.0944, 2.0944, 3.1416, 3.1416, 6.2832, 6.2832, 6.2832 rad/s Torso, eight motor axes in motor-ID order 1–8 0.0349, 0.0349, 0.0698, 0.0698, 0.0698, 0.0873, 0.0873, 0.0873 rad 0.1047, 0.1047, 0.2094, 0.2094, 0.2094, 0.2618, 0.2618, 0.2618 rad 1.0472, 1.0472, 1.0472, 1.0472, 1.0472, 1.5708, 1.5708, 1.5708 rad/s

During catch-up, all axes use the most restrictive axis's increment scaling factor, with a time allowance capped at 20 ms. Catch-up rates apply during catch-up and recovery.

If feedback is no older than 50 ms and the target-to-feedback difference is within the direct threshold, that axis may avoid Hold caused by a large step from the old target; position commands remain subject to catch-up limits. Recovery from Hold requires checked axes to return within the direct threshold or close to that fresh feedback. Hold retains the previous target and existing motion may continue. Torso thresholds are evaluated in motor coordinates.

The robot also checks measured state and hardware faults:

Protection Default setting and behavior Arm feedback position Feedback beyond the position range below expanded outward by 0.0262 rad triggers protection. Application targets must remain within the tabulated position range. Arm position tracking error When position safety checking is active, target-to-feedback error above 0.3491 rad for J1–J4 or 0.6982 rad for J5–J7 triggers fault protection. Arm motor feedback and hardware faults Non-finite feedback, drive faults or motor speed above 8.3776 rad/s for motors 1–3 or 26.7035 rad/s for motors 4–7 trigger fault protection. Chassis command timeout After 100 ms without a valid motion command, the current velocity command expires. Verify standstill using velocity feedback.

After a fault, inspect heartbeat errors and service responses, then follow the recovery procedure. Self-collision checking is disabled by default; applications must plan collision-free motion.

docs.title: Arms
docs.text:
Position targets are clamped per joint as follows. Left and right arms use their respective joint coordinate definitions.

Joint Lower position (rad) Upper position (rad) Joint velocity command clamp (rad/s) J1 -1.6144 4.2673 8.3776 J2 -2.0944 0.3491 8.3776 J3 -1.2217 4.3633 8.3776 J4 -0.1745 2.2689 11.4605 J5 -1.5708 2.6180 22.9210 J6 -1.0472 1.5708 26.7035 J7 -0.8727 0.8727 26.7035

The velocity column caps joint velocity commands. Applications plan operating speeds for the task. SDK Arm APIs accept position targets; motor limits and mechanism pose further affect actual motion.

docs.title: Torso and hands
docs.text:
Torso positions are clamped in the fixed SDK joint order:

Joint J1 J2 J3 J4 J5 J6 J7 J8 Lower (rad) 0 -2.4435 -0.5236 -0.5236 -3.1416 -1.5708 -0.5236 -0.5236 Upper (rad) 1.4835 0 2.0944 0.5236 3.1416 1.5708 0.5236 0.8727

See TorsoClient for joint names and diagram. Combined waist poses must also satisfy mechanism and motor constraints.

Hand limits follow the delivered model's joint table. Default speed and current coefficients are 0.5 and 0.6 respectively; both are dimensionless.

docs.title: Chassis
docs.text:
Parameter Default value Meaning vx / vy acceleration 10 m/s² each Limits body-frame x and y acceleration separately. vtheta angular acceleration 10 rad/s² Yaw velocity slew limit. extension_velocity acceleration 0.5 m/s² Stretch-axis velocity slew limit. Stretch speed 0.05 m/s Stretch synchronization speed cap. Stretch length 0.357–0.477 m Mechanism stretch range; the SDK controls stretch through extension_velocity. Wheel motor speed 31.4159 rad/s Motor cap; closed-loop wheel control caps speed at 20.9440 rad/s. The stricter limit applies. Steering angle ±2.7925 rad Hard limit: ±2.7925 rad. Steering-angle selection uses a ±2.3562 rad soft band.

Steering alignment and stretch state can further reduce wheel speed. Determine vx/vy/vtheta ranges from chassis motion constraints. After sending zero velocity, confirm standstill using velocity feedback.

docs.title: Smoothing continuous position commands
docs.text:
Arms and torso use quintic interpolation to convert streamed position targets into higher-rate control targets. Applications continuously send smooth targets.

Parameter Each arm Torso Control period 1 ms (1000 Hz) 2 ms (500 Hz) Nominal command period 20 ms 20 ms Interpolation velocity parameter 10 rad/s 1.0472 rad/s (motor space) Interpolation acceleration parameter 30 rad/s² 2.0944 rad/s² (motor space)

The nominal period is an interpolation reference and allows variations in send intervals. Larger target changes may extend execution time. Interpolation parameters, catch-up rates and joint velocity limits act at different stages. Applications plan velocity, acceleration and jerk.

The robot connects each segment with a quintic polynomial, matching position, velocity and acceleration at both endpoints:

q(t) = a0 + a1 t + a2 t² + a3 t³ + a4 t⁴ + a5 t⁵,  0 ≤ t ≤ T

Here q is position (rad), T is segment time (s), and the six coefficients are determined by endpoint position, velocity and acceleration. New streamed targets continue from the current motion state.

The figure shows a single segment with zero endpoint velocity and acceleration. With s=t/T, its position is q(t)=q0+(q1−q0)(10s³−15s⁴+6s⁵). Continuous motion uses the actual endpoint derivatives.

Segment time is estimated from the command period and extended for larger target changes:

T0 = clamp(1.5 P, Tc, 0.2 s)
T  = max(T0, 1.875 × max_i |q1[i] − q0[i]| / vmax)

P is the estimated command period, Tc the control period, and vmax a positive interpolation velocity parameter. Position and velocity must use the same coordinate space. The 0.2 s cap applies to timing estimation; actual T may be longer. Velocity and acceleration parameters clamp derivative estimates and outputs. Applications must still check velocity, acceleration and jerk over the complete trajectory.

After a stream stops, the final position is retained and output velocity and acceleration decay within 50 ms. Confirm standstill through device feedback.

Hands receive the latest complete target directly; applications ensure target continuity. Hand feedback without progress for more than 300 ms is marked stale. Existing targets may continue executing after sending stops; confirm standstill through device feedback.

docs.title: Shutdown and reconnect
docs.text: Finish the application task-stop workflow, then close subscriptions and the SDK. close() cancels subscriptions, clears caches and releases this object’s time-sync session. After the last time-sync session closes, the previous system time services are restored. Recreate user subscriptions after reconnecting. Python can use with NorthSDK(config) to connect and close automatically.

docs.title: Shared entry point
docs.text:
C++: create main.cpp containing these includes, one selected example function, then the entry point, in that order. Replace the default master_status(*sdk) call for other examples. Integrate the selected example into your existing C++ application using the delivered public headers and libraries.

#include <north_sdk/NorthSDK.h>
#include <array>
#include <chrono>
#include <iostream>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <thread>
#include <utility>

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    if (argc != 2) {
        std::cerr << "usage: north_sdk_app <endpoint>\n";
        return 2;
    }
    try {
        north::SdkConfig config;
        config.connect_endpoints = {argv[1]};
        auto created = north::NorthSDK::Create(config);
        if (!created) throw std::runtime_error(created.error().message);
        auto sdk = std::move(created.value());
        auto connected = sdk->connect();
        if (!connected) throw std::runtime_error(connected.message());
        master_status(*sdk);
        sdk->close();
    } catch (const std::exception& error) {
        std::cerr << error.what() << '\n';
        return 1;
    }
    return 0;
}

Compile and run using NORTHSDK_PREFIX from Quick Start:

g++ -std=c++17 main.cpp \
  -I"$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/include" -L"$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/lib" -lnorth_sdk \
  -Wl,-rpath,"$NORTHSDK_PREFIX/lib" \
  -o north_sdk_app
./north_sdk_app "$NORTHSDK_ENDPOINT"

Python: create app.py with these imports, one selected example function, then the entry point. Replace the example call in the entry point.

import sys
import time
from north_sdk import (
    NorthSDK, SdkConfig, NorthSDKError, ErrorCode, Side,
    TactileImageKind, PowerDataQuality, MasterResult, LidarSource, LidarPayloadKind,
    OperationMode, CommandChannel, WholeBodyCommand, ArmCommand,
)

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        raise SystemExit("usage: python3 app.py <endpoint>")
    config = SdkConfig()
    config.connect_endpoints = [sys.argv[1]]
    try:
        with NorthSDK(config) as sdk:
            master_status(sdk)  # Replace with one example call from the index.
    except (NorthSDKError, RuntimeError) as error:
        print(error, file=sys.stderr)
        raise SystemExit(1)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

python3 app.py udp/192.168.100.100:7449

docs.title: Read cached left-arm state
docs.text:
Try for up to two seconds to read left-arm state received within 500 ms. The first call may lack data. Retry only kStaleState; valid state prints the position count. Cache reads establish the required state reception automatically.

This example uses a 500 ms cache-age limit and a two-second first-sample wait. Choose values from the device publication period and application latency requirements. See ArmClient::latest_state.

docs.title: C++
docs.text:
void arm_cache(north::NorthSDK& sdk) {
    auto arm = sdk.arm(north::Side::kLeft);
    const auto deadline = std::chrono::steady_clock::now() + std::chrono::seconds(2);
    while (std::chrono::steady_clock::now() < deadline) {
        auto result = arm.latest_state(std::chrono::milliseconds(500));
        if (result) {
            std::cout << "joints=" << result.value().joints.position.size() << '\n';
            return;
        }
        if (result.error().code != north::ErrorCode::kStaleState)
            throw std::runtime_error(result.error().message);
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(50));
    }
    throw std::runtime_error("No fresh left-arm state within 2 seconds");
}

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
def arm_cache(sdk):
    arm = sdk.arm(Side.LEFT)
    deadline = time.monotonic() + 2
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        try:
            state = arm.latest_state(500)
        except NorthSDKError as error:
            if error.code != ErrorCode.STALE_STATE:
                raise
            time.sleep(0.05)
        else:
            print("joints=", len(state.joints.position))
            return
    raise RuntimeError("No fresh left-arm state within 2 seconds")

docs.text: Subscribe to the chassis-front Lidar for five seconds and print the first point of each frame: coordinates in meters and reflectivity. The SDK decompresses Zstd automatically. void lidar_points(north::NorthSDK& sdk) {
    auto result = sdk.sensors().on_lidar(
        north::LidarSource::kChassisFront, [](const north::LidarFrame& frame) {
            auto print_first = [](const auto& groups) {
                for (const auto& group : groups) {
                    if (group.points.empty()) continue;
                    const auto& point = group.points.front();
                    std::cout << "xyz(m)=" << point.x << ',' << point.y << ',' << point.z

                print_first(frame.laser_shots);
            else if (frame.kind == north::LidarPayloadKind::kSubAreas)
                print_first(frame.sub_areas);
        });
    if (!result) throw std::runtime_error(result.error().message);
    auto sub = std::move(result.value());
    std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::seconds(5));
    sub.close();
}

void send_two_arms(north::NorthSDK& sdk, north::CommandChannel channel,
                   const std::array<float, 7>& left,
                   const std::array<float, 7>& right) {
    north::ArmCommand left_command, right_command;
    left_command.joints.position.assign(left.begin(), left.end());
    right_command.joints.position.assign(right.begin(), right.end());
    north::WholeBodyCommand command;
    command.left_arm = left_command;
    command.right_arm = right_command;
    auto sent = sdk.whole_body().send(channel, command);
    if (!sent) throw std::runtime_error(sent.message());
}

    from north_sdk import JointCommand
    left_joints, right_joints = JointCommand(), JointCommand()
    left_joints.position = list(left)
    right_joints.position = list(right)
    left_command.joints = left_joints
    right_command.joints = right_joints
    command = WholeBodyCommand()
    command.left_arm = left_command
    command.right_arm = right_command
    sdk.whole_body().send(channel, command)
